hook: A two-dimensional VO2 PINN may not need more spectral capacity to resolve a pulse-created switching front: at matched total parameter count, a physically constrained local kinetics clock can make the same front slower in the network coordinate while preserving the original electro-thermal-phase equations. The claim is deliberately narrower than a general coordinate-warp advantage and is tested against learned and analytic coordinate transforms as well as the strongest spectral, causal, weighting, and hard-constraint alternatives.

falsification_prediction: Generate a predeclared bank of 2D VO2 pulse-switching trajectories with the named FEniCSx model, then train the kinetics-clock PINN and all matched baselines on the training cases, select only on in-distribution validation, and score locked whole-case OOD afterward. If the mechanism works, switching-time absolute error, phase-front Hausdorff/topology error, energy-balance error, worst normalized coupled residual, and V/T/ξ field error should decrease relative to the unmodified-coordinate arm without a wall-time or memory claim being required. The one load-bearing variable is τψ(x,t), the learned accumulated kinetics clock; the sole negative-control intervention fixes gψ(x,t)=t in nondimensional units while leaving the head, budget, samples, and residual implementation unchanged, and predicts those downstream device metrics return toward the unmodified-coordinate PINN baseline. Failure of the clock arm to beat both that identity control and the learned/analytic coordinate-transform competitors, or failure of the identity intervention to remove the downstream gain, falsifies the claimed kinetics-specific mechanism.
compute_budget: 9.5 80GB-class GPU-days on one GPU for the bounded 2D FEniCSx data generation, matched training arms, three-seed replication, and locked post-selection OOD scoring; $0 paid API.
what_step_was_missed: NeuSA would have needed to replace its single global physical-time coefficient flow with a spatially local monotone clock whose rate is coupled to the endogenous phase-kinetic right-hand side, then re-express the complete electric, heat, and phase residuals under that map rather than assuming a fixed global spectral evolution.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: NeuSA constructs a global truncated spectral state evolved by a NODE for canonical wave problems, whereas this candidate constructs a spatially local, strictly monotone kinetics coordinate jointly constrained by the phase-rate law and evaluates the unchanged VO2 electro-thermal-phase residuals through its full pullback.

The adaptive-spectral study varies Fourier frequencies and initial-condition gates for one stiff ODE, whereas this candidate changes the independent coordinate of a 2D coupled device PDE and retains every time- and space-derivative cross term induced by that local map.

The energy-embedded phase-field PINN obtains steady microstructures by replacing dynamic evolution with a static problem, whereas this candidate retains and scores the full pulse-driven switching trajectory, event timing, moving topology, and energy balance.

The operando VO2 work reveals sub-nanosecond electro-thermo-phase topology dynamics and supplies a physical target regime, whereas this candidate constructs a physics-residual neural coordinate solver whose claim is bounded to synthetic numerical closure rather than experimental validation.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: openalex:W4403443387 (collision_hits). R-adaptive DeepONet already demonstrates that transforming discontinuous PDE solutions from a physical domain to an equidistributed computational domain, then learning the solution and coordinate transformation maps separately, can overcome a sharp-solution representation bottleneck; therefore a broad claim that learned adaptive coordinates themselves resolve fronts is already occupied. The candidate stands only on its narrower result: a spatially local temporal clock constrained by the endogenous phase-kinetic rate, a complete pullback of the unchanged coupled electro-thermal-phase PDE, and a kinetics-specific gain over matched generic learned and analytic transforms. The retrieved pool covered learned/adaptive coordinate transforms and moving-mesh PINNs but showed no exact `Kξ`-driven material-time or reaction-progress-coordinate PINN of this form; that absence is provisional because arXiv and OpenAlex succeeded, Semantic Scholar coverage was partial with some rate-limited queries, and OpenReview was unavailable.
